symptoms.0: The training data is synthetic, generated from a fixed table of diseases and symptoms. Scores show how well the model reproduces that table, not how accurately it identifies illness in real people.
symptoms.1: Only 41 conditions are covered. Your illness may be something not on the list, and the closest match will still be shown.
symptoms.2: Match scores are relative to these 41 conditions and are not the probability that you have a disease.
symptoms.3: Not a diagnosis. Many conditions share symptoms; a doctor's examination and tests are needed.

diabetes.0: Trained only on women of Pima heritage aged 21 or older, a population with very high diabetes prevalence. Results for men, younger people, and Indian populations are extrapolations and may be inaccurate.
diabetes.1: The glucose input is the 2-hour value from an oral glucose tolerance test, not a fasting or random reading.
diabetes.2: Many insulin and skin-fold values are missing in the source data; when you leave optional inputs blank they are filled with typical values.
diabetes.3: Not a diagnosis. Diabetes is diagnosed with laboratory tests such as HbA1c or fasting glucose, interpreted by a clinician.

diabetes_symptoms.0: Collected from people attending a diabetes hospital, so about 62% had diabetes. Real-world prevalence is far lower, so estimates for the general public will tend to be too high.
diabetes_symptoms.1: Many rows in the source data are exact duplicates; they were removed before evaluation, leaving a smaller dataset than its nominal 520 rows.
diabetes_symptoms.2: Symptoms are self-reported yes/no answers; diabetes often has no symptoms in its early stages, so a low estimate does not rule it out.
diabetes_symptoms.3: Not a diagnosis. Diabetes is diagnosed with laboratory tests such as HbA1c or fasting glucose.

heart.0: Trained on 303 patients from one US hospital in the 1980s who had already been referred for angiography — a population with a much higher rate of heart disease than the general public. Estimates for people without symptoms will tend to be too high.
heart.1: Several inputs (maximum heart rate on exercise test, ST depression, fluoroscopy vessel count, thallium scan) come from clinical tests. Missing optional inputs are filled with typical values, which lowers reliability.
heart.2: Sex was recorded as binary in the source data.
heart.3: Not validated on Indian populations. Not a diagnosis.

parkinsons.0: Voice measures are a weak indicator on their own: when tested on people the model had never seen, it missed many people with Parkinson's and wrongly flagged many healthy people (see the measured sensitivity and specificity).
parkinsons.1: The result is not a risk percentage. It shows whether the voice measures look more like the Parkinson's group or the healthy group in one study. Parkinson's is uncommon in the general population, so most people whose voice 'resembles the Parkinson's group' do not have it.
parkinsons.2: Measures depend on the microphone, room and software. Values from a different setup than the study's may be unreliable.
parkinsons.3: Colds, laryngitis, smoking, ageing, and other voice or neurological conditions also change these measures.
parkinsons.4: Cannot diagnose Parkinson's disease, which requires examination by a neurologist.

limits.0: Trained on dermatoscopic images (taken with a skin-surface microscope), mostly of lighter skin types from Europe and Australia. Ordinary phone photos and darker skin tones are different from the training data, so results on them are much less reliable.
limits.1: Covers only 7 kinds of pigmented skin lesions. Rashes, infections, wounds and other skin conditions are outside what the model knows; it will still pick one of the 7 categories.
limits.2: It is not a cancer diagnosis. Only a doctor's examination, often with a biopsy, can diagnose skin cancer. Any changing, bleeding or unusual spot should be checked by a dermatologist regardless of this result.
limits.3: The dataset contains far more ordinary moles than other lesion types; the rarer categories are recognised less reliably (see per-category results).

poha.0: Rinse the flattened rice (poha) in a sieve until soft, then drain.
poha.1: Heat the oil, roast the peanuts, then add chopped onion and green chilli and cook until soft.
poha.2: Add the peas and a pinch of turmeric and cook for 2–3 minutes.
poha.3: Stir in the poha, cover and steam for 2 minutes on low heat.
poha.4: Finish with lemon juice and chopped coriander.

upma.0: Dry-roast the semolina (rava) until it smells nutty, then set aside.
upma.1: Heat the oil, cook the chopped onion, green chilli, carrot and peas until soft.
upma.2: Add about 2½ times as much water as semolina and bring to a boil.
upma.3: Pour in the semolina slowly while stirring, cover and cook on low heat for 3 minutes.

idli_sambar.0: Soak the rice and urad dal separately for 4–6 hours, grind to a batter and ferment overnight.
idli_sambar.1: Steam the batter in greased idli moulds for 10–12 minutes.
idli_sambar.2: For sambar, cook the toor dal until soft and mash it.
idli_sambar.3: Cook the bottle gourd, onion and tomato in a little oil with sambar powder, add the dal and water, and simmer for 10 minutes.

masala_dosa.0: Make a fermented rice and urad dal batter (soak 4–6 hours, grind, ferment overnight).
masala_dosa.1: Boil and mash the potato; cook it briefly with onion, turmeric and a little oil.
masala_dosa.2: Spread a ladle of batter thinly on a hot pan and drizzle a few drops of oil.
masala_dosa.3: When crisp, place the potato filling in the centre and fold.

oats_porridge.0: Bring the milk to a simmer.
oats_porridge.1: Add the oats and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until creamy.
oats_porridge.2: Top with sliced banana and chopped almonds.

besan_chilla.0: Mix the gram flour (besan) with water into a smooth, pourable batter.
besan_chilla.1: Stir in finely chopped onion, tomato and coriander.
besan_chilla.2: Spread the batter on a hot greased pan and cook both sides until golden.

moong_chilla.0: Soak the moong dal for 3–4 hours and grind to a smooth batter.
moong_chilla.1: Mix in chopped onion, green chilli and coriander.
moong_chilla.2: Spread thin on a hot greased pan and cook both sides until golden.

aloo_paratha_curd.0: Knead the wheat flour with water into a soft dough.
aloo_paratha_curd.1: Mash the boiled potato with spices for the filling.
aloo_paratha_curd.2: Fill a ball of dough with the potato, roll out gently and cook on a hot pan with a little oil on both sides.

egg_bhurji_toast.0: Heat the oil and cook the chopped onion and tomato until soft.
egg_bhurji_toast.1: Add the beaten eggs and stir gently until just set.

boiled_eggs_fruit.0: Boil the eggs for 9–10 minutes, cool in water and peel.
boiled_eggs_fruit.1: Serve with the apple, sliced, and the toast.

sprouts_salad.0: Steam the sprouted moong for 3–4 minutes (or use raw if you prefer).
sprouts_salad.1: Mix with chopped onion, tomato and cucumber.
sprouts_salad.2: Add lemon juice and a pinch of salt and chaat masala.

millet_porridge.0: Cook the millet (or ragi flour) in water until soft, stirring often.
millet_porridge.1: Add the milk and simmer for 2–3 minutes.
millet_porridge.2: Sweeten lightly with the sugar and top with chopped almonds.

tofu_scramble_toast.1: Heat the oil, cook the chopped onion and tomato, then add the tofu with turmeric.
tofu_scramble_toast.2: Cook for 3–4 minutes and serve with toast.

peanut_butter_toast.1: Spread the peanut butter and top with sliced banana.

dal_rice.0: Pressure-cook the toor dal with water and turmeric until soft, then mash.
dal_rice.1: Heat the oil, add cumin and mustard seeds, then the chopped onion and tomato.
dal_rice.2: Add the cooked dal and simmer for 5 minutes.

rajma_rice.0: Soak the kidney beans overnight and pressure-cook until very soft.
rajma_rice.1: Cook the chopped onion and tomato in the oil with spices to a thick gravy.
rajma_rice.2: Add the beans with some cooking water and simmer for 10 minutes.

chole_roti.0: Soak the chickpeas overnight and pressure-cook until soft.
chole_roti.1: Cook the onion and tomato in the oil with chole masala.
chole_roti.2: Add the chickpeas and simmer until the gravy thickens.

palak_paneer_roti.0: Blanch the spinach for 2 minutes, cool and blend to a purée.
palak_paneer_roti.1: Cook the onion and tomato in the oil with spices.
palak_paneer_roti.2: Add the spinach purée and simmer for 5 minutes, then add the paneer cubes.

veg_pulao_raita.0: Rinse the rice. Heat the oil, add whole spices and the vegetables and sauté for 2 minutes.
veg_pulao_raita.1: Add the rice and water (about 1:2), cover and cook until done.
veg_pulao_raita.2: For the raita, mix the curd with grated cucumber and a pinch of roasted cumin.

mixed_veg_dal_roti.0: Cook the masoor dal with turmeric until soft.
mixed_veg_dal_roti.1: Add the chopped cauliflower, carrot and peas and cook until tender.
mixed_veg_dal_roti.2: Temper with cumin in the oil and pour over the dal.

sambar_rice.0: Cook the toor dal until soft and mash.
sambar_rice.1: Cook the bottle gourd, okra and tomato in a little water with sambar powder and tamarind.
sambar_rice.2: Add the dal, simmer for 10 minutes and temper with mustard seeds in the oil.

curd_rice.0: Cook the rice until soft and let it cool slightly.
curd_rice.1: Mix in the curd and chopped cucumber.
curd_rice.2: Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in the oil and stir in.

moong_khichdi.0: Rinse the rice and moong dal together.
moong_khichdi.1: Pressure-cook with the carrot, peas, turmeric and about 4 times as much water until soft.
moong_khichdi.2: Stir in the ghee before serving.

bhindi_dal_roti.0: Cook the masoor dal with turmeric until soft and season.
bhindi_dal_roti.1: Slice the okra and stir-fry in the oil with the onion until tender and not sticky.

aloo_gobi_roti.0: Cut the potato and cauliflower into small pieces.
aloo_gobi_roti.1: Cook the onion and tomato in the oil with turmeric and spices, then add the vegetables.
aloo_gobi_roti.2: Cover and cook on low heat until tender.

baingan_bharta_roti.0: Roast the brinjal over a flame or in the oven until soft, then peel and mash.
baingan_bharta_roti.1: Cook the onion and tomato in the oil, add the mashed brinjal and cook for 5 minutes.
baingan_bharta_roti.2: Serve with roti and the cooked dal.

chicken_curry_rice.0: Marinate the chicken in the curd and spices for 30 minutes.
chicken_curry_rice.1: Cook the onion and tomato in the oil until soft.
chicken_curry_rice.2: Add the chicken and cook covered for 20–25 minutes until fully cooked.

fish_curry_rice.0: Cook the onion and tomato in the oil with turmeric and chilli.
fish_curry_rice.1: Add the coconut (ground or as milk) and a little water and bring to a simmer.
fish_curry_rice.2: Add the fish pieces and cook gently for 8–10 minutes until cooked through.

egg_curry_roti.1: Cook the onion and tomato in the oil with spices to make a gravy.
egg_curry_roti.2: Add the eggs, simmer for 5 minutes and serve with roti.

tofu_peas_curry_rice.1: Cook the onion and tomato in the oil with spices, then add the peas and a little water.
tofu_peas_curry_rice.2: Add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes. Serve with the rice.

grilled_chicken_salad.0: Season the chicken and grill or pan-cook with a little oil until fully cooked.
grilled_chicken_salad.1: Slice and toss with the cucumber, tomato and cabbage.
grilled_chicken_salad.2: Dress with lemon juice and serve with the bread.

rajma_brown_rice.0: Soak the kidney beans overnight and pressure-cook until very soft.
rajma_brown_rice.1: Cook the onion and tomato in the oil with spices, add the beans and simmer.

millet_khichdi.0: Rinse the millet and moong dal.
millet_khichdi.1: Pressure-cook with the carrot, beans, turmeric and water until soft.
millet_khichdi.2: Stir in the ghee before serving.

veg_soup_toast.0: Chop the carrot, cabbage, beans and tomato.
veg_soup_toast.1: Simmer with the moong dal in water for 15–20 minutes, then season (blend if you like).

paneer_bhurji_roti.1: Cook the onion, tomato and peas in the oil, then add the paneer with turmeric.
paneer_bhurji_roti.2: Cook for 2–3 minutes and serve with roti.

mushroom_matar_roti.1: Cook the onion and tomato in the oil with spices, then add the mushrooms and peas.
mushroom_matar_roti.2: Cook until the mushrooms are tender and serve with roti.

lauki_chana_dal_rice.0: Soak the chana dal for 1 hour.
lauki_chana_dal_rice.1: Pressure-cook with the chopped bottle gourd, tomato and turmeric until soft.
lauki_chana_dal_rice.2: Temper with cumin in the oil and serve with the rice.

fruit_bowl.0: Wash and cut the papaya and apple; add the pomegranate seeds.

roasted_peanuts.0: Dry-roast the peanuts in a pan for 5–6 minutes, stirring, or buy unsalted roasted peanuts.

almonds.0: Eat as they are, or soak overnight and peel.

buttermilk.0: Whisk the curd with about twice as much cold water.
buttermilk.1: Add a pinch of roasted cumin and salt.

boiled_corn.0: Boil or steam the corn for 8–10 minutes.
boiled_corn.1: Add lemon juice and a pinch of salt.

sweet_potato_chaat.0: Boil or roast the sweet potato until soft, then peel and cube.
sweet_potato_chaat.1: Add lemon juice and chaat masala.

yogurt_fruit.0: Mix the curd with the sliced banana.

sesame_peanut_mix.0: Dry-roast the sesame seeds and peanuts separately and mix.

health_extra.allergiesHint: Include allergies and any foods you don't eat (e.g. curd, dal, brinjal), separated by commas. Diet plans will leave them out.

doctors.id: Infectious-disease specialist or government ART centre

precautions.0: Wash your face twice a day with a mild cleanser; don't scrub hard.
precautions.1: Don't squeeze or pick pimples — it causes scars and infection.
precautions.2: Use oil-free, non-comedogenic skin and hair products.
precautions.3: Change pillow covers often and keep hair off the face.

acne.urgent: Painful deep lumps, scarring, or acne that is affecting your mood.

precautions.0: Get an HIV test — testing and treatment (ART) are free at government ART centres.
precautions.1: Use condoms and never share needles, razors or syringes.
precautions.2: If you've had a recent possible exposure, see a doctor within 72 hours about preventive medicine (PEP).
precautions.3: If diagnosed, take treatment every day exactly as prescribed — it allows a long, healthy life.

aids.urgent: High fever, breathlessness, severe weight loss or confusion.

precautions.0: Stop drinking alcohol completely — this is the most important step; ask your doctor for help with withdrawal.
precautions.1: Eat regular, nutritious meals.
precautions.2: Don't take painkillers or herbal remedies without a doctor's advice.
precautions.3: Get liver tests done as your doctor advises.

alcoholic_hepatitis.urgent: Vomiting blood, black stools, confusion or extreme sleepiness, or a swollen belly.

precautions.0: Notice and avoid your triggers (dust, pollen, certain foods, pets).
precautions.1: Keep your home dust-free; wash bedding in hot water weekly.
precautions.2: Keep windows closed on high-pollen or dusty days.
precautions.3: Carry your prescribed medicine if you have had severe reactions before.

allergy.urgent: Swelling of the lips, tongue or throat, difficulty breathing, or fainting — call 112.

precautions.0: Stay active with gentle exercise like walking, swimming or yoga.
precautions.1: Keep a healthy weight to reduce load on joints.
precautions.2: Use warm compresses for stiffness.
precautions.3: Don't take painkillers regularly without a doctor's advice.

arthritis.urgent: A hot, red, very swollen joint with fever.

precautions.0: Always carry your inhaler and learn the correct technique.
precautions.1: Avoid smoke, dust, strong smells and cold air; don't smoke.
precautions.2: Take preventer medicine regularly if prescribed, even when you feel well.
precautions.3: Get the yearly flu vaccine if your doctor advises.

asthma.urgent: Breathlessness that makes speaking hard, blue lips, or no relief from the inhaler — call 112.

precautions.0: Get up slowly from bed — sit for a minute before standing.
precautions.1: Avoid sudden head movements and looking up for long.
precautions.2: Sleep with your head slightly raised.
precautions.3: Ask a doctor about repositioning exercises (for example, the Epley manoeuvre).

bppv.urgent: Dizziness with severe headache, weakness, slurred speech, double vision or trouble walking — call 112.

precautions.0: This is an emergency: call 112 or go to the nearest hospital immediately.
precautions.1: Note the time the symptoms started — it matters for treatment.
precautions.2: Don't give food, drink or medicine by mouth.
precautions.3: Keep the person lying on their side if they are drowsy or vomiting.

brain_hemorrhage.urgent: Any sudden weakness of one side, slurred speech, severe headache or loss of consciousness.

precautions.0: Keep a good posture; raise screens to eye level.
precautions.1: Take breaks from phones and computers to stretch the neck.
precautions.2: Use a firm, low pillow.
precautions.3: Do neck exercises shown by a physiotherapist.

cervical_spondylosis.urgent: Weakness or numbness in the arms or legs, or loss of bladder or bowel control.

precautions.0: Stay home until all the blisters have crusted (usually 5–7 days) to avoid infecting others.
precautions.1: Don't scratch; keep nails short and use calamine lotion for itching.
precautions.2: Drink plenty of fluids.
precautions.3: Don't give aspirin to children. Keep away from pregnant women and newborns.

chicken_pox.urgent: Breathlessness, a very high fever, drowsiness, or infected (red, painful, pus-filled) blisters.

precautions.0: See a liver specialist for tests to find the cause.
precautions.1: Avoid alcohol.
precautions.2: Eat a low-fat, balanced diet.
precautions.3: Don't take herbal or over-the-counter medicines without a doctor's advice.

chronic_cholestasis.urgent: Fever with chills, severe belly pain, or confusion.

precautions.0: Rest and drink plenty of warm fluids.
precautions.1: Steam inhalation and salt-water gargles can ease symptoms.
precautions.2: Wash hands often and cover coughs and sneezes.
precautions.3: Antibiotics do not help a cold — don't take them without a prescription.

common_cold.urgent: Breathlessness, fever above 3 days, or symptoms lasting more than 10 days.

precautions.0: Get a blood test (NS1 / platelet count) as advised by a doctor.
precautions.1: Rest and drink plenty of fluids (ORS, coconut water, soups).
precautions.2: Take only paracetamol for fever — avoid ibuprofen, aspirin and other painkillers.
precautions.3: Prevent mosquito bites: nets, repellent, and no stagnant water near home.

dengue.urgent: Severe belly pain, repeated vomiting, bleeding gums or nose, black stools, or feeling very weak or drowsy — go to hospital.

precautions.0: Check your blood sugar as your doctor advises.
precautions.1: Eat regular, balanced meals; limit sugar, sweets and refined flour.
precautions.2: Walk or exercise at least 30 minutes most days.
precautions.3: Check your feet daily and get eyes and kidneys tested yearly.

diabetes.urgent: Very high or very low sugar with confusion, vomiting or fast breathing.

precautions.0: Stop the suspected medicine only after speaking to a doctor.
precautions.1: Note the medicine's name and tell every doctor about it in future.
precautions.2: Don't take any new medicine without a prescription.
precautions.3: Use cool compresses for itching.

drug_reaction.urgent: Swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty, or a rash with blisters or peeling skin — call 112.

precautions.0: Keep the affected area clean and fully dry.
precautions.1: Wear loose cotton clothes and change socks and innerwear daily.
precautions.2: Don't share towels, combs or clothes.
precautions.3: Don't use steroid creams without a doctor's advice — they make fungal infections worse.

fungal_infection.urgent: Spreading infection, fever, or no improvement after 2 weeks.

precautions.0: Drink ORS frequently in small sips to prevent dehydration.
precautions.1: Eat light food like rice, banana, curd or khichdi once you can.
precautions.2: Wash hands with soap after using the toilet and before eating.
precautions.3: Drink safe (boiled or filtered) water.

gastroenteritis.urgent: Blood in stools, no urine for 8 hours, severe weakness, or a child who is very drowsy.

precautions.0: Eat smaller meals and don't lie down within 2–3 hours of eating.
precautions.1: Raise the head end of your bed.
precautions.2: Limit spicy, oily food, tea/coffee and alcohol; stop smoking.
precautions.3: Keep a healthy weight.

gerd.urgent: Chest pain (rule out a heart problem), difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood or black stools.

precautions.0: This is an emergency: call 112 or go to the nearest hospital immediately.
precautions.1: Stop all activity and sit or lie down.
precautions.2: Don't drive yourself to the hospital.
precautions.3: If you're not allergic, chewing one regular aspirin may help — ask the emergency operator.

heart_attack.urgent: Chest pain or pressure, pain in the arm or jaw, sweating or breathlessness.

precautions.0: Eat high-fibre food (vegetables, fruits, whole grains) and drink plenty of water.
precautions.1: Don't strain or sit on the toilet for long.
precautions.2: Warm water sitz baths can ease pain.
precautions.3: Stay active.

hemorrhoids.urgent: Heavy bleeding, or bleeding with dizziness or weakness.

precautions.0: Rest and eat light, nutritious food.
precautions.1: Avoid alcohol and don't take painkillers without a doctor's advice.
precautions.2: Drink only boiled or filtered water and wash hands well.
precautions.3: Keep separate utensils and towels until recovery.

hepatitis_a.urgent: Confusion, extreme sleepiness, bleeding, or yellowing that keeps getting worse.

precautions.0: See a liver specialist for tests and follow-up — it can be managed with treatment.
precautions.1: Avoid alcohol completely.
precautions.2: Don't share razors, toothbrushes or needles; use condoms.
precautions.3: Family members should get tested and vaccinated.

hepatitis_b.urgent: Confusion, vomiting blood, black stools, or a swollen belly.

precautions.0: See a liver specialist — hepatitis C can usually be cured with medicine.
precautions.1: Avoid alcohol completely.
precautions.2: Don't share needles, razors or toothbrushes.
precautions.3: Get liver tests done as advised.

hepatitis_c.urgent: Confusion, vomiting blood, black stools, or a swollen belly.

precautions.0: See a liver specialist for tests and treatment.
precautions.1: Avoid alcohol completely.
precautions.2: Don't share needles, razors or toothbrushes; use condoms.
precautions.3: Hepatitis B vaccination protects family members from hepatitis D too.

hepatitis_d.urgent: Confusion, vomiting blood, black stools, or a swollen belly.

precautions.0: Rest and drink plenty of safe fluids.
precautions.1: Drink only boiled or filtered water; avoid street food during recovery.
precautions.2: Avoid alcohol and painkillers without a doctor's advice.
precautions.3: Pregnant women need urgent medical care — hepatitis E can be serious in pregnancy.

hepatitis_e.urgent: Confusion, bleeding, or any symptoms during pregnancy.

precautions.0: Check your blood pressure regularly.
precautions.1: Reduce salt, pickles, papad and packaged foods.
precautions.2: Exercise at least 30 minutes most days and keep a healthy weight.
precautions.3: Don't stop prescribed medicine on your own, even if you feel fine.

hypertension.urgent: Severe headache, chest pain, breathlessness, blurred vision or weakness on one side — call 112.

precautions.0: Get thyroid blood tests and see an endocrinologist.
precautions.1: Limit tea, coffee and other stimulants.
precautions.2: Take medicine regularly as prescribed and get follow-up tests.
precautions.3: Eat enough to keep your weight stable.

hyperthyroidism.urgent: Very fast or irregular heartbeat, high fever, confusion or fainting.

precautions.0: If conscious, immediately take 15 g of fast sugar (3 teaspoons of sugar or glucose in water, or a glass of fruit juice), then recheck in 15 minutes.
precautions.1: Then eat a proper snack or meal.
precautions.2: If you take diabetes medicine, carry sugar or glucose with you at all times.
precautions.3: Don't skip meals or exercise heavily on an empty stomach.

hypoglycemia.urgent: Unconsciousness, seizures, or inability to swallow — call 112; don't give food by mouth.

precautions.0: Get thyroid blood tests and see an endocrinologist.
precautions.1: Take thyroid medicine on an empty stomach every morning, as prescribed.
precautions.2: Get thyroid levels checked as advised.
precautions.3: Stay active and eat a balanced diet.

hypothyroidism.urgent: Extreme sleepiness, confusion or very slow heartbeat.

precautions.0: Gently wash the sores with soap and water and keep them covered.
precautions.1: Don't scratch; keep nails short.
precautions.2: Don't share towels or clothes; wash them in hot water.
precautions.3: Keep children home until a doctor says they're no longer contagious.

impetigo.urgent: Fever, spreading redness, or sores that don't improve with treatment.

precautions.0: Get blood tests to find the cause — jaundice is a sign, not a disease.
precautions.1: Rest, drink plenty of safe water and eat light food.
precautions.2: Avoid alcohol and don't take herbal or local remedies without a doctor.
precautions.3: Don't take painkillers without a doctor's advice.

jaundice.urgent: Confusion, extreme sleepiness, bleeding, severe belly pain, or in a newborn baby.

precautions.0: Get a blood test for malaria the same day — treatment works best when started early.
precautions.1: Complete the full course of medicine prescribed.
precautions.2: Prevent mosquito bites: nets, repellent, full-sleeve clothes.
precautions.3: Remove stagnant water near your home.

malaria.urgent: Confusion, fits, very high fever, breathing difficulty, or dark urine — go to hospital.

precautions.0: Keep a headache diary to find your triggers (lack of sleep, skipped meals, stress, bright light).
precautions.1: Sleep and eat at regular times; drink enough water.
precautions.2: Rest in a dark, quiet room during an attack.
precautions.3: Don't use painkillers more than 2–3 days a week without a doctor's advice.

migraine.urgent: The worst headache of your life, sudden headache with weakness, confusion or fever — call 112.

precautions.0: Do regular low-impact exercise like walking or cycling.
precautions.1: Keep a healthy weight.
precautions.2: Use supportive footwear and a walking stick if needed.
precautions.3: Physiotherapy exercises help strengthen muscles around the joint.

osteoarthritis.urgent: A suddenly swollen, hot joint or inability to bear weight.

precautions.0: Eat regular meals; avoid spicy food, alcohol and smoking.
precautions.1: Avoid painkillers like ibuprofen or aspirin unless a doctor says so.
precautions.2: Get tested for H. pylori infection as advised.
precautions.3: Complete the full course of medicine prescribed.

peptic_ulcer.urgent: Vomiting blood, black stools, or sudden severe belly pain — go to hospital.

precautions.0: See a doctor soon — pneumonia often needs prescribed antibiotics and a chest X-ray.
precautions.1: Rest and drink plenty of fluids.
precautions.2: Complete the full course of medicine.
precautions.3: Older adults and those with long-term illness can ask about pneumonia and flu vaccines.

pneumonia.urgent: Breathlessness, chest pain, confusion, or blue lips — go to hospital.

precautions.0: Moisturise your skin daily.
precautions.1: Avoid skin injuries, very hot water and harsh soaps.
precautions.2: Manage stress; avoid smoking and alcohol.
precautions.3: Use medicines only as prescribed by a dermatologist.

psoriasis.urgent: Widespread redness of the skin, fever, or painful swollen joints.

precautions.0: Get a sputum test — testing and treatment are free under the national TB programme.
precautions.1: Take the full course of medicine (at least 6 months) without missing doses.
precautions.2: Cover your mouth when coughing and keep rooms well ventilated.
precautions.3: Eat nutritious food; avoid smoking and alcohol.

tuberculosis.urgent: Coughing up blood, breathlessness or chest pain.

precautions.0: See a doctor for a blood test and the right antibiotics.
precautions.1: Complete the full course of medicine, even if you feel better.
precautions.2: Drink only boiled or filtered water; eat freshly cooked food.
precautions.3: Wash hands with soap before eating and after the toilet.

typhoid.urgent: Severe belly pain, blood in stools, confusion, or fever lasting more than a week.

precautions.0: Drink plenty of water.
precautions.1: Don't hold urine for long.
precautions.2: Keep the genital area clean; wipe front to back.
precautions.3: See a doctor for a urine test — UTIs usually need prescribed antibiotics.

uti.urgent: Fever with back pain, vomiting, or blood in urine; any UTI during pregnancy.

precautions.0: Avoid standing or sitting for long periods; take short walks.
precautions.1: Raise your legs when resting.
precautions.2: Compression stockings can help — ask a doctor which kind.
precautions.3: Exercise regularly and keep a healthy weight.

varicose_veins.urgent: A painful, swollen, red or warm leg (possible clot), or bleeding from a vein.
